# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)

# Main Street story-line adapter does not apply option cost/extraEffect

**Headline:** The Main Street story-line engine adapter omits the core `applyResourceDelta` seam, so option `cost` and `extraEffect` are never charged or applied.

Discovered-from: `MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY` (cost-aware event-choice over the core presented option list).

## Problem

Core `@story-line` resolves an option's declarative `cost` and `extraEffect` through the engine adapter's optional `applyResourceDelta` seam (`core/src/story-line/resolve.ts`). A legacy adapter without it is left untouched and appends the activity-log line *"Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied: the engine adapter does not implement applyResourceDelta."*

`mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` (`src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts`) implements `rng`, `applyEffect`, `getResources`, `appendLog`, `getActivityLog`, `getTemplate`, `getBaseTypeId`, `getChainScanCards` and `pushChainCard` — but **not** `applyResourceDelta`.

Consequences:

- A cost-gated option is filtered out of the presented list at draw time (`isOptionAffordable`), yet a *presented* cost option is never actually charged — so affordability never changes after paying.
- `extraEffect` deltas silently never land (options are inert where content expects a bonus/penalty).
- Any card using a cost or extra effect pollutes the activity log with the warning line above.

## Impact

Until this is fixed, the AI cost-aware policy (`MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY`) scores costs that the engine never collects and effects that never apply. The AI unit contract can still be satisfied (projection is a pure function), but end-to-end play with cost-bearing options is incorrect.

Secondary gap (same story, narrower): CSV `options` authoring has no syntax for `cost`/`extraEffect`, and `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` `#/definitions/option` carries only `label`/`successorIds`/`effectPolicy`. So content cannot yet declare a cost — only registered options can. Authoring support should be its own item once enforcement exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` implements `applyResourceDelta(state, delta)`, applying `coins` and `reputation` deltas to `state.resourceBank` and keeping the ledger/score view consistent (same sync path `resolveEventOption` uses, e.g. `syncResourceBankToLedger`).
- A unit test proves a cost-bearing option deducts exactly `cost.coins`/`cost.reputation` on resolution, for both `effectPolicy: 'apply'` and `'skip'`.
- A unit test proves `extraEffect` deltas are applied for both effect policies, and that the resolution result's `coinChange`/`repChange` reports cost + extra effect + (for `apply`) the card effect.
- An integration test resolves a pending cost choice headlessly and asserts the activity log contains **no** "Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied" line.
- Undo of a resolved paid choice (snapshot command) restores the pre-payment resources; save/load round-trip preserves the post-payment balance.
- Existing behaviour with cost-free options is unchanged (storyline regression harness green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `applyResourceDelta` to the adapter, delegating to the existing state resource helpers and the ledger sync one-liner.
- Follow the settlement order documented in core: card effect (per `effectPolicy`) → cost → extra effect.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts` — add `applyResourceDelta`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` settlement/ledger sync + log assertions
- `src/MainStreetState.ts` — `resourceBank` and ledger sync helpers
- `core/src/story-line/resolve.ts` — settlement order and warning contract (read-only)
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts` — resolution test home

## Notes

- `core/` is a pinned submodule — no core changes expected; if core needs a signature change, raise it as a core (`CG-`) item instead.

# Per-turn loan repayment in the closing sequence

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the loan model slice.

## Goal

As a player holding a loan, exactly `perTurnRepayment` coins leave my wallet at the end of
every turn for `termTurns` turns, the deduction shows up in the turn's net summary as an
expense, and the loan then disappears.

## Context

- Turn economy closes in `processEndOfTurn` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`): income,
  staff/community/business ongoing costs, then the incident, then `appendTurnNetRow`.
  Repayment belongs in that same sequence so the net row reflects it.
- Turn net rows are written by `appendTurnNetRow` (delta summary + totals lines) and the
  `TurnResult` carries an optional `turnLedger` (MS-0MVP45KZV006TMUK) with one-off deltas —
  prefer extending that ledger so the Turn Summary dialog can surface the expense rather
  than adding a parallel channel.
- Competitive seats keep their wallet in `state.players[].coins` with
  `state.resourceBank` as the working mirror (`bindCompetitiveSeat` /
  `restoreCompetitiveSeat`); single-player has no `state.players`. Repayment must work for
  whichever wallet is active, and must not disturb the other seats in a competitive close.
- Producer Q6=A: repayment is deducted unconditionally — a shortfall leaves `coins < 0` and
  the ordinary bankruptcy path decides what happens next. The bailout offer itself is the
  next slice; this slice must not add an offer.

## Desired change

1. `applyLoanRepayments(state)` in `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`: for each active loan, debit
   `perTurnRepayment` through the ledger/wallet path, decrement `turnsRemaining`, remove the
   loan when `turnsRemaining` reaches 0, and log a one-off expense row.
2. Call it in `processEndOfTurn` after the incident resolution and **before** the
   end-condition checks, for both the deferred and the legacy paths, and include the
   repayment in the pending/turn ledger deltas.
3. Keep `loansEnabled: false` a hard no-op (no log rows, no ledger entries) so the headless
   baseline stays byte-identical.
4. Tests: three-turn schedule for 600/6 (110 per turn, 660 total), retirement after
   `termTurns` (no seventh deduction), ledger/net-row expense entry, unclamped deduction
   leaving `coins < 0`, and a loans-disabled no-op.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At the end of every turn in which a seat holds an active loan, exactly `perTurnRepayment` coins are deducted from that seat's wallet and the deduction is recorded in the turn's net summary as a one-off expense.
- The loan is retired after `termTurns` payments and no further deductions occur.
- Repayment is deducted unconditionally: a payment that exceeds the seat's balance leaves coins < 0 and triggers the normal bankruptcy path, so a seat already repaying a loan receives no new bailout offer.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — `applyLoanRepayments` and repayment logging
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — call site ahead of the end-condition checks, ledger wiring
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — repayment line on `TurnResult.turnLedger`
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` — activity-log helper (if a new effect class is needed)
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanBailout.test.ts` — new repayment tests

# Wire Bank Loan button into the Turn Summary dialog

Follow-up raised by the Bank Loans planning session (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG), per producer
decision Q4: the Turn Summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) has landed, so its deliberately
disabled **Bank Loan** affordance can now be wired to the loan feature.

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary dialog shows an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** button and never calls
the `onBankLoanAction` seam reserved for the loans feature, so a mid-game player has no
entry point to credit at all — the loan engine only surfaces offers on bankruptcy. This item
turns the reserved affordance into a working mid-game loan entry point, with no new engine
rules.

## Users

- **Mid-game human player (single-player)** — "When the Turn Summary dialog is on screen
  and I am short of cash, I want to borrow from the configured loan menu so I can fund the
  next week's move, and I want to see the repayment schedule before I commit."
- **Cautious player** — "I want the button to tell me *why* it is unavailable (loans turned
  off, or I already owe money) instead of a generic 'coming soon' note."

Not a user of this slice: competitive seats (per-seat closing text, no summary dialog),
AI seats (bailout-only policy — no proactive loans).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Enabled/disabled matrix.** The Bank Loan button is interactive only when
   `state.config.loansEnabled === true` **and** the acting (human) seat holds no active loan;
   in every other case it is rendered disabled (muted, `input` disabled) with a hint that
   explains the reason.
2. **Selector with schedule.** Pressing the enabled button opens the loan selector listing
   every configured `config.loanOptions` entry with its per-turn repayment and total
   repayment, plus a way to back out; backing out returns to the Turn Summary dialog with no
   state change.
3. **Confirm dispatches `takeLoan`.** Confirming an option dispatches the `takeLoan` command
   for the acting seat, credits the principal to that seat's wallet, records the active loan,
   and leaves `actionsRemaining` unchanged.
4. **No day advance.** Neither opening the selector nor confirming a loan advances the day or
   resumes the deferred closing; the day advances only on **[ Next Turn ]**, exactly once.
5. **Refreshed dialog.** After the loan is taken the Turn Summary dialog is re-rendered from
   the same `TurnResult` with the post-`takeLoan` state, so the new obligation is visible and
   the button is now disabled (one-active-loan rule) while **[ Next Turn ]** still works.
6. **Testing/validation.** Tests cover the enabled/disabled matrix (loans enabled + no loan,
   active loan, `loansEnabled: false`), the selector content, the `takeLoan` dispatch, the
   no-action-point rule, the cancel path, and that the day does not advance before
   **[ Next Turn ]**.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments (`showTurnSummaryDialog`, the gate, the button-construction site),
   `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (the "[ Bank Loan ] is always disabled" paragraph), and the
   in-game help/loan documentation touched by MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` renders `[ Bank Loan ]` with `disableInteractive()`, colour
  `#6b6459`, and the hint *“Bank loans are not available yet — coming in a future update.”*;
  it explicitly does `void onBankLoanAction` so the seam can never fire. `BANK_LOAN_HINT` is
  duplicated in `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`, whose AC4 asserts
  "always disabled, seam never invoked" — that test must be rewritten, not deleted.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` delegates to `msOverlayManager`; with no overlay manager (headless) it
  calls `onNextTurn()` immediately so the closing is never stranded.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `shouldGateTurnSummary()` restricts the
  dialog to `requiresDeferredClosing` single-player closings (never replay, reduced motion,
  tutorial or competitive); `presentTurnSummaryGate()` builds the summary with
  `buildTurnSummary(s.state, result)` and calls
  `s.showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn)` — the third argument is not passed today.
- Overlays already read live state (`s.state.config` in `MainStreetOverlayContent`), so
  `loansEnabled` needs no new plumbing into the scene.
- `buildTurnSummary()` is Phaser-free and read-only, so re-rendering after a loan only needs
  the same `state` + `result` pair re-run.
- **The loan engine does not exist yet.** `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `config.loansEnabled`,
  `config.loanOptions`, the `takeLoan` command and `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` are
  all still unimplemented: the Bank Loans epic MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG sits at
  `intake_complete`, its slices are `blocked` (only the headless determinism baseline,
  MS-0MVPWS45N008PR0X, is in flight). This item is the epic's only out-of-epic follow-up and
  must land *after* the model, `takeLoan`, and overlay-UI slices.
- Save schema v3 (loans + pending offer) is delivered by the epic; this slice must not touch
  serialisation.

## Desired change

1. **Carry a loans descriptor into the dialog.** Extend the gate's call so the dialog receives
   one small Phaser-free descriptor rather than reaching into scene state ad hoc — predicted
   shape `{ enabled: boolean; activeLoan: { perTurnRepayment, turnsRemaining } | null;
   options: LoanOption[] }` built in `presentTurnSummaryGate()` from `s.state.config` and the
   acting seat. Keeps the overlay presentation-only and the descriptor unit-testable.
   (Implementation may instead read `s.state` directly if the epic's helpers make that
   cleaner — the ACs do not care which; see Assumptions.)
2. **Enable the affordance** when `enabled && activeLoan === null`, wiring `pointerdown` to
   the `onBankLoanAction` seam; keep the button disabled otherwise with a reason-specific
   hint (loans disabled vs. already owing — see open question Q3).
3. **Loan selector** presented on press: reuse the epic's `MainStreetLoanOverlay` option rows
   (per-turn + total repayment). The epic builds it for a *pending offer* driven by
   `state.pendingLoanOffer`; this slice needs a non-bailout mode (no pending offer, options
   from `config.loanOptions`, Cancel/back instead of Decline). Reusing the row renderer, not
   duplicating it, is the requirement; a small `mode` parameter is expected.
4. **Confirm = dispatch.** Confirming dispatches the `takeLoan` command through the existing
   command surface (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`), never mutating state inline.
5. **Refresh in place** after a successful take: rebuild the summary from the same
   `TurnResult` and re-render the dialog (dismiss the old overlay objects first so
   `s.overlayObjects` stays consistent), leaving `[ Next Turn ]` as the only way to resume
   `advanceTurn`.
6. **Tests** in a new `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` (browser
   overlay, mirroring `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` helpers) plus the rewrite of the
   dialog suite's AC4 case.

## Constraints

- **Presentation wiring only** — no new engine rules, no changes to the loan model, repayment
  maths or one-active-loan validation; those belong to MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
- **No action point cost** and **no day advance** — taking a loan from the dialog must leave
  `actionsRemaining` untouched and must not resume the deferred closing.
- **Single-player deferred path only** — the dialog itself is gated to that path; competitive
  per-seat closing and the tutorial/reduced-motion/replay paths are unchanged.
- **Overlay conventions** (`core` UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` +
  `createOverlayButton`, all elements parented into `s.hudContainer` and pushed to
  `s.overlayObjects`, depths 199/200/201, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), SFX via
  `safePlaySound`.
- **Blocked-by sequencing** — depends on MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (dependency edge already
  recorded): specifically the loan model/config slice (MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB), the `takeLoan`
  command slice (MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79) and the overlay-UI slice (MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA).

## Assumptions

- **A1 First repayment falls on the next turn's closing.** The closing sequence (and its
  ledger) has already run when the dialog is presented, so a loan taken at the dialog must not
  charge a repayment against the turn being summarised. Recorded as OPEN QUESTION Q1 for
  producer confirmation.
- **A2 Proactive loans are allowed at any coin balance** — the button is not gated on
  affordability or negative coins (the goal is mid-game credit, not a second bailout path).
- **A3 The selector's rows come from `config.loanOptions`**, so a re-balanced menu needs no UI
  change, and the dialog is unavailable (button disabled) when the menu is empty.
- **A4 `takeLoan` rejection is surfaced, not swallowed** — if the engine refuses (e.g. a race
  into an active loan), the dialog shows the engine's reason and stays open rather than
  silently closing.
- **A5 Headless safety is untouched** — with no overlay manager the scene still calls
  `onNextTurn()`; the new descriptor must remain optional so existing call sites compile.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Sequencing risk (highest):** the epic is not implemented; starting this slice early would
  mean inventing engine helpers (scope creep). Mitigation: keep the item dependency-blocked
  until the three prerequisites are `completed`.
- **Duplicated overlay logic:** copy-pasting the bailout overlay instead of parameterising it
  would leave two loan selectors to maintain. Mitigation: AC2/desired-change 3 require reusing
  the epic's row renderer.
- **Stale dialog content:** re-rendering from a mutated `state` but a stale `TurnResult` can
  show a mismatch. Mitigation: rebuild via `buildTurnSummary(state, result)` with the same
  `result` object (the ledger is presentation data, not recomputed).
- **Overlay object leak:** dismissing and re-rendering must reset `s.overlayObjects` the same
  way `dismissOverlay` does, or duplicated buttons accumulate in `hudContainer`. Mitigation:
  explicit test asserting a single `[ Next Turn ]`/`[ Bank Loan ]` pair after a refresh.
- **Test drift:** `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` AC4 encodes "always disabled"; leaving
  it untouched makes the suite self-contradictory. Mitigation: rewrite that case in the same
  commit.
- **Scope creep:** competitive-mode parity (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI), AI proactive loans, multiple
  loans, loan repayment UI polish — record as linked work items, do not fold in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — enable/disable `[ Bank Loan ]`, wire the seam,
  render the reason-specific hint and refresh the dialog after a take.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — build and pass the loans descriptor in
  `presentTurnSummaryGate()`; keep `shouldGateTurnSummary()` unchanged.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — pass the descriptor through the delegation method.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — reuse the epic's option rows in a non-bailout
  (mid-game select) mode.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — consume `activeLoanFor` / option-table helpers (read-only use).
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoan` command dispatch and the no-AP assertion.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` — **new.** Wiring tests.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` — rewrite the "seam never invoked"
  case.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — update the "always disabled" Turn Summary paragraph.

## Out of scope / non-goals

- Competitive-mode summary dialog and any competitive loan entry point
  (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI).
- Engine rules: repayment timing, bailout offer loop, AI policy, persistence — owned by
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
- HUD obligation readout (MS-0MVPWSCRD004A6Z4) and the loans help/documentation slice
  (MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB); this item only edits the one doc paragraph it invalidates.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** (Bank Loans, epic, `intake_complete`) — the engine this slice wires

- **MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB** (Loan model, config and repayment maths), **MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79**

- **MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT** (Overlay: turn summary dialog + browser test, completed) — created

- **MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R** (deferred closing gate, completed) — the gate that presents the

- **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI** (End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode, open) — the other

  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`,
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (repayment timing): "A loan taken from the Turn Summary dialog — when does the first
  repayment hit? (A) at the next turn's closing, since this turn's closing and ledger have
  already run [recommended]; (B) immediately when the deferred closing resumes, so the turn

- Q4 (proactive eligibility): "Is the button available at any balance, or only when the seat

# Bumping the engine pin to core dev tip breaks the unit suite (phaser window is not defined)

## Problem statement

`npm run build` runs `engine:sync`, which advances the `./core` submodule and
`configs/engine-pin.json` to the core `dev` tip. At the current tip
(`34e0ab6d`, CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB) the unit suite dies at collection time —
23 suites pull in `@ui` (via `src/scenes/…` → `@ui/shakeIllegalMove`), whose
new `illegalMoveToastView` → `Renderer` chain value-imports `phaser`, and
Phaser's device detection touches `window` under node
(`ReferenceError: window is not defined`, `phaser/src/device/OS.js`). A normal
build therefore leaves a red tree that the dev-push pre-push hook refuses, and
the workaround in use pins core behind the tip.

## Users

- **Game developer in this repo** — must be able to `npm run build` and then
  `npm test` on the resulting pin with both green, without manual
  `git -C core checkout …` gymnastics or offline `engine:sync` fallbacks.
- **Dev-push gate / audit** — a green full-suite cache entry must be producible
  at the pinned engine, or no work item can reach `in_review` (`implement.py
  finish` runs the build, which re-pins to the tip).

User stories:

- As a developer, I can run `npm run build` followed by `npm test` on the
  composed pin, and both pass, so I never have to remember the pinned-commit
  workaround.
- As the release line, I can `engine:verify` the recorded pin because the pin
  sha resolves on core `dev`, so release builds are reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — engine checkout consistent:** `npm run engine:check` passes: the
  `./core` checkout equals `configs/engine-pin.json` sha equals the `core`
  gitlink at HEAD; the Vitest root preflight no longer aborts every project
  ("project unit executed 0 of 388 expected file(s)").
- **AC2 — unit suite green at the tip:** with the pin at the current core `dev`
  tip, `npm test` (unit + unit-cli via the test skill) passes with **zero**
  `window is not defined` collection errors, and the full project suite
  (including browser) passes at the new pin.
- **AC3 — no per-file mock shim:** the green result does not come from adding
  `vi.mock('phaser')` / `vi.mock('@ui/…')` to the 23 affected test files purely
  to survive the core import chain; a node-environment regression guard covers
  the affected core import chain (`@ui/shakeIllegalMove` → `illegalMoveToastView`
  / `Renderer`) — either this repo's guard or the engine-side guard from
  CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ.
- **AC4 — pin movement attributable:** the re-pin (`core` gitlink advance +
  `configs/engine-pin.json` sha change, both staged together) is its own commit
  whose message names this item and the engine commit consumed; no feature work
  is mixed in.
- **AC5 — documentation:** all related documentation and code comments are
  updated — `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (pin policy, offline fallback),
  `docs/dev/testing.md` (engine-checkout preflight), any workaround notes in
  commit messages/comments describing the 0409c1eb hold — to reflect the new
  pin and the removed workaround.

## Constraints

- **Engine-side fix is upstream, not here.** The `@ui` barrel change belongs to
  the core repo and is already tracked: CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ (open). This item
  must not duplicate that code change inside `./core`; it consumes it via
  re-pin. The one allowed local alternative, if the producer elects it at
  review, is a node-safe Phaser stub alias scoped to the `unit`/`unit-cli`
  Vitest projects only (see Desired change §4) — acceptable but inferior
  because it fixes only this repo.
- **Pin + gitlink travel together** (CG-0MVO268500071BPI): one actor, one
  moment, one commit — a re-pin commit can never record them divergent, and the
  offline `engine:sync` fallback must NOT be used for this transition (it would
  silently keep the stale pin).
- **Push policy:** dev only. **Implement worktree requirement** applies at
  implementation time (`implement.py start/finish`, worktree isolation,

# Intake brief: Dev-session browser console errors — `/api/transcripts` 404 and the dev-server drop cascade

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical · **Cross-repo:** yes (`Tableau-Card-Engine` core + this repo) · **Discovered-from:** operator report (dev session, `vite --host` on `:3000`)

## Problem statement

A normal Main Street dev session fills the browser console with errors: every game-over `POST /api/transcripts` returns **HTTP 404** (the transcript persistence middleware exists in the engine but is never registered by this repo's generated `vite.config.ts`), and when the dev server dies mid-session the page floods with `[vite] server connection lost`, failed HMR WebSocket retries and `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` for all ~180 card SVG assets. The operator requirement is a clean dev-session console: no HTTP 404s from the app's own endpoints, no repeated warnings for expected conditions, and a documented, diagnosable signature (with evidence) for the two error classes that are not app defects.

## Users

- **Developers/agents running `npm run dev`** — must get a clean console so genuine errors are visible.
  - *User story:* "As a developer working on Main Street, I want a dev session where the console shows no 404s or error-class noise from the app, so that a red line in the console always means something is actually broken."
- **Anyone reading a session transcript / browser log for diagnosis** (agents auditing console output, the operator triaging a report) — must be able to tell app defects from environment/infrastructure artefacts.
  - *User story:* "As an operator triaging a pasted console log, I want each error class to be either fixed or explicitly documented as out-of-scope with a diagnostic procedure, so that I don't re-file it as a bug."
- **Core template maintainers** (Tableau-Card-Engine) — every scaffolded game repo must start with dev transcript persistence wired, so a re-scaffold cannot regress it.
  - *User story:* "As a core maintainer, I want `renderViteConfig` to emit the transcript-persist registration, so new game repos never ship a 404-ing `/api/transcripts`."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No `/api/transcripts` 404 in a dev session.** With `npm run dev` running, a game-over transcript save issues `POST /api/transcripts` and receives **HTTP 200**, and `data/transcripts/<gameType>/<gameType>-<ISO-timestamp>.json` is written; the browser console shows no `[TranscriptStore] Disk persistence POST returned HTTP 404`. Guarded by an automated test that loads the real `vite.config.ts` factory for `command: 'serve'` and asserts the `transcript-persist` plugin **is** registered, and is **not** registered when `process.env.VITEST` is set (mirroring `core/tests/vite-config.test.ts`), plus an in-process dev-server smoke that POSTs to `/api/transcripts` and asserts 200 + file creation under a temp `destRoot`.
2. **Scaffold template carries the same guard.** `renderViteConfig` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` emits the `transcriptPersistPlugin()` registration (dev-serve only, `!process.env.VITEST`-gated), and a core test asserts both the **rendered source** and the **on-disk generated** `vite.config.ts` contain it — so a `npm run scaffold` re-run cannot silently drop it (same pattern as the `resolve.dedupe` guard, MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL).
3. **Expected-condition logging is quiet.** The disk-persistence path issues its request only where the endpoint can exist (`import.meta.env.DEV`) and logs a non-2xx/missing-endpoint outcome **at most once per session at `console.debug`/`info`** — never a repeated `warn` for an expected absence — and the `csv-checksum.json` fetch-miss in `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign` is downgraded the same way. Verified by unit tests asserting (a) at most one log call across repeated saves/failures, (b) no `console.warn`/`console.error` emitted on the expected-miss path.
4. **The two non-app error classes are resolved by evidence, not silence.** (a) `Uncaught (in promise) Error: A listener indicated an asynchronous response…` is verified to originate from a browser extension: an extension-free Chromium run of the existing Vitest `browser` project (whose `tests/e2e/main-street-no-console-errors.browser.test.ts` asserts a clean console on boot) produces no such error, and the finding is recorded in the work item as **out-of-scope with evidence**. (b) The dev-server-drop cascade (`[vite] server connection lost`, repeated `WebSocket connection to ws://<host>:3000/ failed`, `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` for every card SVG / `csv-checksum.json`) is documented in a dev-server troubleshooting section of `docs/dev/testing.md` with: its signature; the fast triage (`ss -ltn | grep :3000` — no listener means the server is gone, not that assets are missing; the same assets return 200 from a live server); the likely causes on this host (swap exhaustion / memory pressure — 7.3 GB of 8 GB swap in use at report time, many `.worklog` worktrees, concurrent sibling dev servers and browser suites); and the remediation. Any host-level remediation is tracked in a linked follow-up item, not in app code.
5. **Tests and docs.** Changed-scope test gate green during implementation and the full project test suite green before the dev push; `docs/dev/testing.md` (and the `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Transcript Persistence cross-reference, if the core contract changes) updated — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo:** the template half lives in the `core` submodule (`Tableau-Card-Engine`), which needs its own `CG-…` work item; this repo's `configs/engine-pin.json` pin must move after the core change lands (see MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV for the pin/lag rules, and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — a core worktree checkout lags the pin by design).
- **`vite.config.ts` is auto-generated** by the scaffold template; never hand-edit it without also changing `renderViteConfig`, or the next re-scaffold drops the fix.
- **Keep the VITEST gate.** The plugin intentionally does no file-system side effects during test runs (`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Transcript Persistence); the fix must not register it under `VITEST`.
- **No new runtime dependencies**; no change to the on-disk transcript contract (`data/transcripts/<game>/…`, consumed by `scripts/replay.ts` / `scripts/export-transcripts.ts`).
- **Do not weaken console assertions** as a way of passing: the e2e console guard must stay a real guard (adjusting benign-pattern lists is only acceptable for third-party/browser noise with recorded justification).

## Existing state

- `core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` exports `transcriptPersistPlugin()` + a bounded `POST /api/transcripts` handler (body cap, rate limit, atomic-ish write to `data/transcripts/`) — the middleware is correct and battle-tested in core.
- `core/vite.config.ts` registers it: `...(command === 'serve' && !process.env.VITEST ? [transcriptPersistPlugin()] : [])`.
- **This repo's `vite.config.ts` imports only `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`** from that module and never registers the plugin — verified live: a fresh `vite --port 3000` session returns `HTTP 404` for `POST /api/transcripts` while `/`, every card SVG and `csv-checksum.json` return `HTTP 200`.
- `core/src/core-engine/transcript/TranscriptStore.ts` → `postToDisk()` fire-and-forgets `fetch('/api/transcripts')` and `console.warn`s on any non-OK response — so every game-over logs a 404 warn whenever the plugin is absent (dev misconfiguration, Vitest browser mode, production build, Electron).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts` (~L230) `console.warn`s on a `csv-checksum.json` fetch throw.
- The dev-server drop is environmental: swap is 7.3 GB / 8 GB consumed on this host, 23 `.worklog` worktrees exist, and sibling repos (`AI_Hell`, `Tableau-Card-Engine`) were running their own `vite --host` dev servers plus a browser test suite concurrently at the time of the report. `docs/dev/testing.md` already documents the analogous ENOSPC/environmental class and its triage (reference MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C) — same treatment applies here.
- `installHook.js` appears in the operator's stack traces; this repo has no React and no `chrome.runtime` usage, so the message-channel error is extension-origin.

## Desired change

1. Register `transcriptPersistPlugin()` in this repo's `vite.config.ts`, gated on dev-serve and not under `VITEST` (the config factory callback must take `command`).
2. Mirror that registration in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderViteConfig` (core repo, own `CG-…` item) + a core template guard test.
3. Add a game-repo guard test for the registration contract (serve vs VITEST) and, for real coverage of the wiring, an in-process dev-server smoke asserting `POST /api/transcripts` → 200 with a temp `destRoot`.
4. Make expected-condition logging quiet and once-per-session: gate `postToDisk` on `import.meta.env.DEV`, and downgrade the non-2xx/miss path plus the `csv-checksum.json` fetch miss to a single debug/info log.
5. Document the dev-server-drop signature, triage steps and likely causes in `docs/dev/testing.md`; record the extension-origin verification for the message-channel error; file/link a follow-up for host remediation if the kill cause proves host-level.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `vite.config.ts` — import `transcriptPersistPlugin`; take `command` in the factory; register it dev-serve-only behind `!process.env.VITEST`
- `tests/tooling/vite-transcript-plugin-registration.test.ts` — **new** guard (plugin present for `serve`, absent under `VITEST`) + in-process dev-server smoke POST → 200 + file written
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderViteConfig` emits the registration (core repo change)
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — assert rendered template **and** on-disk generated config carry the registration (core repo)
- `core/src/core-engine/transcript/TranscriptStore.ts` — `postToDisk`: `import.meta.env.DEV` gate + log-once at debug/info
- `tests/core-engine/transcript/TranscriptStore.test.ts` (core) — log-volume assertions (≤1 log across repeated failures; no warn on expected path)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts` — `csv-checksum.json` fetch-miss `console.warn` → `console.debug`
- `tests/e2e/main-street-no-console-errors.browser.test.ts` — extend/confirm it also covers the transcript-persistence path (no 404 warn, no message-channel error)
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — new "dev server died: WS failures + `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`" troubleshooting section (signature, triage, causes, remediation)
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — § Transcript Persistence cross-reference for the game-repo registration contract (only if the contract text changes)

## Related work

- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** (completed) — *Scaffold template must emit `resolve.dedupe` in generated `vite.config.ts`*: the exact cross-repo precedent for this fix (generated file + `renderViteConfig` + template guard), including how the core work item and pin bump were handled.
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** (completed) — *Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs*: the established pattern for classifying a dev-server failure as environmental and documenting (not coding around) it.
- **MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C** (completed) — the ENOSPC troubleshooting entry in `docs/dev/testing.md` that the new dev-server-drop section should mirror in tone and structure.
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** (open, low) — *Port Vite watcher-ignore (`server.watch.ignored`) to sibling game repos' generated `vite.config.ts`*: same "generated config drift" family; this item's template change should be reviewed against it so the two template edits do not conflict.
- **MS-0MV26MOWT004ZCQC** (completed) — *Console noise when running the tutorial (tf factory + zone collision warnings)*: prior art for "console must be clean" as a testable contract.
- **MS-0MUTU19SF007791K** (completed) — *Avoid duplicate Main Street card SVG regeneration on game start*: explains the `Regenerated N card SVGs` info lines (and why 175 vs 185 is a card-pack/CSV change, not an error).
- **MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0** (open) — *Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos*: touch-point if the template is regenerated/inspected here.
- Docs: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Transcript Persistence (endpoint contract + VITEST/rate-limit rationale); `docs/dev/testing.md` (troubleshooting section conventions); `core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` (module doc-comment: memory-safety bounds, `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — template drift (high impact, low likelihood once guarded):** editing only this repo's generated `vite.config.ts` leaves the next `npm run scaffold` broken. *Mitigation:* template change + template guard test in core (AC2).
- **Risk — cross-repo sequencing:** the core change needs its own `CG-…` item and a pin bump here; doing the game-repo half first means a transient period where `core` lags. *Mitigation:* land the core template change first, then re-pin and regenerate (MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV rules); document the order in the child items.
- **Risk — silencing real errors:** downgrading logs can hide genuine failures. *Mitigation:* log-once at debug/info, keep an error-level log for *unexpected* failures (non-DEV builds, 5xx), and assert the distinction in tests.
- **Risk — Vitest browser mode hits the same 404 path** (`VITEST` disables the plugin) and could newly fail a console-clean assertion. *Mitigation:* the `import.meta.env.DEV` gate removes the request entirely under test/prod builds; assert it in the unit test rather than adding the 404 to a benign list.
- **Risk — scope creep into host remediation** (swap pressure, orphaned dev servers, 23 worktrees). *Mitigation:* per operator decision this item documents + diagnoses only; host remediation becomes a linked follow-up item (`machine-hygiene` domain).
- **Assumption:** the operator's browser has a devtools-type extension loaded (evidence: `installHook.js` in the stack); the message-channel error therefore cannot be eliminated from app code and is closed by verification + documentation (AC4a).
- **Assumption:** no product code currently depends on transcript disk persistence; the fix restores a dev-only convenience plus a console-hygiene contract.
- **Out of scope (record as follow-ups, not scope):** a dev-server supervisor/auto-restart wrapper; swapping this host's workloads; a general console-error lint gate for all dev sessions; the 175→185 SVG count difference (card-pack activation, not an error).

- **Q2: Cross-repo core template fix** — fix this repo's `vite.config.ts` and the core scaffold template, or game-repo only?

- **Q3: The extension message-channel error** — verify it is extension-origin in a clean Chromium and record as out-of-scope, or must this item eliminate it regardless of origin?
  - **Answer (operator): verify + record.** Source: interactive reply (`wl reviewed` round 1).
  - Research: `installHook.js` is a browser-extension hook; this repo has no React and no `chrome.runtime` usage; the extension-free `browser` project boots the game cleanly.

expense detail. Per-seat ongoing costs are computed today in

# Per-seat net change, closing balances and incident/one-off parity

## Goal

Round out each competitive seat row with the figures single-player already shows:
net coin / reputation / score change for the day, the closing coin / reputation /
score balances, and that seat's share of the resolved incident and one-off
deltas — so a competitive player can compare standing properly, not just income.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The competitive round ledger carries, per seat: `netCoinChange`, `netRepChange`, `netScoreChange`, the seat's incident coin/reputation delta, and its one-off coin/reputation delta — all engine-computed, optional and absent-safe.
2. The identity `day-start snapshot + net == closing balance` holds per seat, and each seat's closing coins / reputation / score equals its committed `PlayerRecord` wallet after the closing (asserted against a real engine run, not hand-built fixtures).
3. The model exposes those values on each competitive row (net change, closing balances, incident and one-off deltas), and `null`/absent ledger data degrades to the existing row shape rather than throwing.
4. The panel renders per-seat net change and closing balances (coins / reputation / score) alongside the incident and one-off deltas, matching the single-player column ordering and signed formatting.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (engine reconciliation identity, model row values, panel rendering); single-player output is unchanged.

## Test-first checklist

- **Engine** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` — reconciliation identity per seat across two seeds; closing balances equal `PlayerRecord` wallets; an eliminated seat contributes no row.
- **Model** `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` — net and closing values per row; incident/one-off per row; absent optional deltas degrade gracefully.
- **Panel** competitive panel test — net change and closing balances rendered per seat.

## Minimal implementation

1. Extend the competitive ledger entry (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`) with the net, closing and incident/one-off fields.
2. Populate them where the competitive closing already knows the per-seat wallets and shared incident (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`; the per-owner incident routing already exists via `applyCompetitiveEventEffects`).
3. Expose the values on the competitive row builder in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`.
4. Render them in the panel (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`).

## Key Files:

## Goal

## Goal

Prove — with automated tests — that a remote pack catalogue is discovered,
cryptographically verified, and safely degraded when anything goes wrong, so
the parent's discovery, degradation, rejection and integrity criteria are
met by evidence rather than assertion.

Verification-only: this item adds or hardens tests and fixtures; it does not
add production behaviour. Where a test exposes a real gap in the remote
source, record the gap and raise a comment on the sibling feature item rather
than implementing the fix here.

Coverage to establish:

1. **Discovery.** A pack catalogue served from a configured host appears in

   listing empty when a bundled pack exists.

# Verification: remote pack precedence, gating & asset parity

## Goal

Prove that remote packs are indistinguishable from bundled packs at the
registry, gating and asset layers, and that precedence is deterministic, so the
parent's parity, precedence and asset-resolution criteria are evidenced by
automated tests.

production behaviour. Gaps found are reported on the sibling feature items.

Coverage to establish:

1. **Precedence — bundled wins.** A pack id present in both the bundled and a
   remote source is served from the bundled source, byte-for-byte.
2. **Precedence — remote first-wins.** Two remote sources carrying the same
   pack id resolve to the first-registered source's content.
3. **Registry composition.** The composed registry order is bundled first,
   then remote sources in configured URL order; registration is idempotent by

# Remote pack degradation & bounded timeout hardening

## Goal

As a player, I want the game to always start and play on bundled packs when the
remote host is slow, hung, unreachable or serving rubbish, so that remote
hosting can never block boot or leave me with an empty Card Packs panel.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 3 and 4; parent scope items 5 and 7;
parent constraint "bounded timeout"; locked decision Q3).

## Context

The tracer bullet proves the happy path. This slice hardens the failure paths,
which is where the parent's risk register concentrates (boot latency, offline
regression). All of it is end-to-end observable: the game boots, bundled cards
deal, the listing is non-empty, and the console shows exactly one actionable
warning per rejected source.

## Scope

- Enforce the hard ≈3 s timeout on **every** remote request (manifest and each
  pack CSV), with the abort timer always cleared so no handle leaks.
- Degrade to bundled content — never throw, never blank the listing — for:
  unreachable host, connection rejection, non-2xx status, timeout abort,
  unparseable manifest JSON, wrong manifest schema/version, and a manifest
  entry with no readable `cards` file.
- Per-pack isolation: one unreadable CSV degrades only that pack, so other
  packs from the same source still load.
- Explicit "no client-side caching" behaviour: the source writes nothing to
  `localStorage` / Cache Storage and re-fetches on each boot.
- Warning quality: one warning per rejected source and one per failed pack,
  naming the source/pack and the reason.

## Design notes

- The timeout is per request, so a hung manifest does not consume the budget of
  every CSV read.
- Tests use injected `fetch` and fake timers throughout: no real network, no
  real 3-second waits.
- The bounded-timeout default (3000 ms) is a single exported constant so the
  documentation and the tests reference one value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad
- [ ] A hard timeout (default 3000 ms, exported constant, overridable) is applied to every remote request and abort is enforced with `AbortController`; a fake-timer test asserts the default value and that a hung request resolves `null` at the deadline.
- [ ] The abort timer is cleared on every path (success, error, timeout), asserted with fake timers and a settled request so no dangling handle remains.
- [ ] An unreachable host, a rejected `fetch`, a non-2xx response, a timeout and an unparseable manifest each complete boot on bundled content with exactly one warning and no throw.
- [ ] A manifest with an unexpected schema or version, or listing a pack whose `cards` file is missing, is rejected whole with one warning.
- [ ] A single unreadable CSV resolves `null` for that pack only; another pack CSV from the same source still resolves and its cards still merge.
- [ ] A pack whose CSV header is wrong, or whose card ids duplicate an already-accepted pack, is rejected without affecting packs from other sources.
- [ ] The Card Packs listing input is non-empty when a bundled pack exists and the remote source fails (asserted by a test).
- [ ] A test asserts the remote path performs no `localStorage` or Cache Storage writes (no client-side caching this iteration).
- [ ] Warnings name the offending source and/or pack and the failure reason; asserted for each failure mode.

# Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence

## Goal

As a player, I want a remote pack to never override bundled core content, and
deterministic behaviour when two remote catalogues offer the same pack, so that
remote hosting cannot silently replace or corrupt the game's own packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 5; parent scope items 2 and 3; parent
constraint "additive"; locked decision Q4).

## Context

`PackSourceRegistry` is first-wins by consultation order and `add()` never
reorders. Precedence is therefore *derived from composition order*. The tracer
bullet composed one remote source; this slice makes composition a first-class,
explicitly ordered function that supports several remote catalogues, and pins
the precedence guarantees with tests.

Equally important: the change must remain **inert** for the Electron
content-directory path and for an unconfigured build.

## Scope

- Compose several remote sources additively in configured URL order, always
  after the bundled source.
- Guarantee and test: bundled wins over remote (byte-for-byte); between remote
  sources the first registered wins.
- Idempotent, order-preserving composition; re-adding a duplicate source id is a
  no-op.
- Resilience: a remote source that cannot be constructed is skipped with a
  warning; bundled content still serves.
- Inertness: configuration unset, and the Electron content-directory path, both
  behave exactly as before (no remote source, no remote fetch).
- Gating is untouched — remote packs flow through the unchanged
  `composeContentUnlockEntitlement` resolver, so nothing is automatically
  ungated.

## Design notes

- Composition is a distinct, explicitly named entry point beside
  `createDefaultPackSourceRegistry`; the latter keeps its bundled-only meaning
  so existing callers and tests are unaffected.
- One place decides source order, mirroring the module's existing contract that
  "the registry is the single place source order is decided".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
- [ ] A composition function (e.g. `createConfiguredPackSourceRegistry(config)`) returns a registry whose `sources` order is exactly the bundled source followed by each configured remote source in configured URL order.
- [ ] `createDefaultPackSourceRegistry()` remains bundled-only; existing registry behaviour and tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] A test asserts bundled content wins when the bundled and a remote source both carry the same pack path (byte-for-byte comparison).
- [ ] A test asserts a pack id offered by two remote sources resolves to the first-registered source content.
- [ ] Composition is idempotent: composing twice, or adding a source with a duplicate id, creates no duplicate and reorders nothing.
- [ ] A remote source that throws during construction is skipped with a warning and the bundled source still serves content.
- [ ] With configuration unset, the browser boot path yields a result identical to the bundled-only build.
- [ ] With an explicit launcher `contentDir`, no remote source is composed and no remote fetch occurs (asserted with a spy `fetch`).
- [ ] A remote pack cards reach the applied pool through `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` when configured.
- [ ] An unentitled remote pack is reported `locked`; no ungating shortcut is introduced.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts`
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `src/createMainStreetGame.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackPrecedence.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/PackSourceRegistry.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Ordered, multi-source composition with explicit precedence guarantees.
- Tests for precedence, idempotence, resilience and inertness.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.

# Remote pack asset resolution

## Goal

As a player, I want a remote pack's card art to render correctly, so that a
remote pack looks and plays exactly like a bundled pack.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 7; parent scope item 1; related work
`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` — pack assets self-contained).

## Context

`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` made pack art travel with the pack: the loader produces
`tce-packs://` asset URLs, `resolvePackFileUrl` maps them through the registry,
and pack art is registered from `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`. A bundled source
answers with a same-origin Vite `?url`; a remote source must answer with an
absolute URL on the configured remote base, and only for assets the verified
manifest declares.

This is a vertical slice: registry resolution → loader `assetUrls` → the pack
art registry → the rendered card texture.

## Scope

- Implement `resolvePackFileUrl(path)` on the remote source, returning
  `<base>/packs/<path>` for assets declared by the verified manifest.
- Gate resolution on successful manifest verification: a rejected source
  resolves no assets.
- Reject paths that escape the packs root (traversal) or are not declared by the
  manifest.
- Verify the resolved URL reaches `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` and the pack art
  registry so a remote pack's art is available before textures are generated.

## Design notes

- URL joining must respect a base URL with a path component (a catalogue may be
  hosted under a prefix) and must not double or drop slashes.
- The source returns a URL only; the existing asset-byte transport performs the
  fetch, so the remote source adds no new byte-reading path.
- No caching of asset URLs across boots (consistent with "no client-side
  caching this iteration").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
- [ ] The remote source implements `resolvePackFileUrl(path)` returning an absolute URL on the configured remote base for an asset declared by the verified manifest.
- [ ] A base URL carrying a path prefix (e.g. `https://host/packs-v2/`) is joined correctly; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A rejected source (failed signature or malformed manifest) resolves no asset URLs.
- [ ] An asset path not declared in the manifest, and a path containing `..` or a backslash traversal, resolves `null`.
- [ ] An integration test asserts a remote pack `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` entry is the remote absolute URL and that pack art registration receives it.
- [ ] A remote pack with art renders in the browser pack path, covered by an asset-resolution assertion or a browser test.
- [ ] The source does not add a new asset byte-read path; the existing `fetchAsset` transport still performs the read.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `resolvePackFileUrl` on the remote source
- `src/MainStreetCardPackArt.ts` — pack art registration seam
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackAssets.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Remote asset URL resolution gated on manifest verification.
- Tests covering URL shape, prefix joining, gating and traversal rejection.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.

# Remote pack gating & behaviour parity

## Goal

As a player, I want remote packs to lock, purchase, enable, deal and persist
exactly like bundled packs, so that hosting a pack remotely changes where it
comes from and nothing else.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 2 and 4; parent scope item 4).

## Context

Content-unlock gating is data-driven: `MAIN_STREET_CONTENT_UNLOCK_GATED_PACKS`
declares which packs are gated and `composeContentUnlockEntitlement` plugs into
the loader's `resolveEntitlement` seam. Remote packs must flow through that same
resolver unchanged — the remote source contributes *content*, never
*entitlement*. This slice proves that and covers the interactive flow end to
end.

## Scope

- Confirm an entitled remote pack loads and its cards merge; an unentitled
  remote pack is `locked` and contributes no rows.
- Confirm the scoped simulated purchase (`purchaseMainStreetCardPack`) unlocks a
  declared remote pack, re-discovers it with the same transports, and that the
  pack's cards then merge and deal.
- Confirm enable/disable parity (`applyEnabledMainStreetPacks`), including the
  refusal when a live card instance would be stranded.
- Confirm save/load round-trip parity: the active remote pack set and merged
  checksum are persisted and restored.
- Introduce no ungating shortcut: the remote source must not bypass or relax
  `resolveEntitlement`.

## Design notes

- The pack id a remote catalogue publishes is the entitlement key, exactly as
  for a bundled pack (`dlc:<gameId>:<packId>`). A remote pack that is not
  declared in the gating table keeps the default (Steam-DLC / declared-unlock)
  behaviour — it is never implicitly free.
- This slice is test-and-wiring only where the parity already holds; any real
  gap found becomes a fix here because parity is the parent's AC2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Parity.** Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across the full
- [ ] A test asserts an entitled remote pack is loaded by `loadMainStreetCardPacks` and its cards appear in the merged pool.
- [ ] A test asserts an unentitled remote pack is reported in `locked` and contributes zero merged rows.
- [ ] A test asserts `purchaseMainStreetCardPack` unlocks a declared remote pack, re-discovers it, and returns `purchased: true`, with the pack cards merged afterwards.
- [ ] A test asserts the scoped purchase evaluates only the declared pack purchase rule (no collateral unlocks).
- [ ] A test asserts a save/load round-trip preserves the remote pack active set (id plus version) and merged checksum.
- [ ] A test asserts enabling and disabling a remote pack re-merges the pool, and that disabling is refused while one of its cards is live in state.
- [ ] A test asserts the remote source never supplies or overrides an entitlement; gating remains owned by `composeContentUnlockEntitlement`.
- [ ] The full pack flow (lock, purchase, enable, deal) is covered for a remote pack by automated tests.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts`
- `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackGatingParity.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Gating and interactive-flow parity for remote packs, evidenced by tests.
- Gaps found in parity closed at the wiring level (never by relaxing gating).

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.
- Depends on *Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence*.

# Documentation: remote pack hosting contract

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a written contract for hosting a remote pack
catalogue — where the files go, how the manifest is signed, what the game does
when it cannot verify or reach the host — so that I can publish packs without
reading the source code.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 8, parent scope item 8).

## Scope

- **Configuration** — `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`,
  that they are build-time (changing a URL requires a rebuild), and that
  multiple URLs compose in order.
- **Hosting layout** — the exact URL paths the game requests:
  `<base>/packs/manifest.json`, `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`,
  `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/assets/…`. A worked example tree is required.
- **Signing contract** — the signed envelope shape, the canonical payload bytes
  (including key ordering and whitespace rules), the algorithm (Ed25519) and
  the key separation rule: the private key is held by the operator and never
  shipped in the game. Include a worked example and the verification outcome
  table.
- **Degradation semantics** — the ≈3 s bounded timeout, console-warning-only
  degradation, bundled-wins precedence, no client-side caching, and that
  bundled packs remain the offline story.
- **Licence-clean requirement** — remote pack content must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs.

## Design notes

- Documentation-only slice: it consumes the contract implemented by the
  sibling feature items and must not introduce new behaviour.
- The verification outcome table must match the verifier's discriminated
  results exactly (`ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` /
  `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable`), so operators can map a console warning
  to a cause.
- Explicitly list the recorded follow-ups (signing tooling, client-side
  caching, runtime/launcher URL configuration) so operators know what is not
  in this iteration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
- [ ] `packs/README.md` documents the remote catalogue layout with a worked URL tree, and states that a hosted catalogue uses the same `manifest.json` shape as the bundled packs plus the signature.
- [ ] The signed-envelope shape and canonical payload rules are documented with a worked example an operator can reproduce, and every verifier failure reason is listed with its meaning.
- [ ] `./DEPLOYMENT.md` (or a linked page under `docs/`) documents `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`, the rebuild-to-change rule, and multiple-URL ordering.
- [ ] Degradation semantics are documented: about 3 s timeout, console warning only, bundled always wins, no UI change, no client-side caching.
- [ ] The signing key separation rule is stated: the private key never ships; only the public key is pinned at build time.
- [ ] The licence-clean requirement for remote pack content is stated.
- [ ] The out-of-scope follow-ups (signing tooling, caching, runtime URL configuration) are recorded as follow-ups, not documented as available.
- [ ] Existing documentation tests still pass and the new sections are reachable from the README.

## Key Files

- `packs/README.md`
- `./DEPLOYMENT.md`
- `./README.md`
- `docs/index.md`

## Deliverables

- The hosting contract documentation for distribution operators.
- A verification-outcome table mapping warnings to causes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.
- Depends on *Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence*.
- Depends on *Remote pack asset resolution*.
